text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear opening claim against driverless cars","quality":"position clarity","description":"It states a definite stance early and keeps that position visible throughout the essay."},{"evidence":"boredom, accidents, teen drivers, blame","quality":"argument development","description":"It gives multiple reasons and expands them into a fuller line of reasoning rather than mostly listing points."},{"evidence":"\"if an accident would happen, who would get blamed\" and later \"what would happen to the teenagers\"","quality":"rhetorical questioning","description":"It uses questions to push the reader toward the writer’s concerns and make the argument feel more interactive."},{"evidence":"\"the car may just not be ready for the streets\"","quality":"counterpoint awareness","description":"It acknowledges a practical limitation of the technology instead of only repeating a single fear."},{"evidence":"teenagers \"would probably not get enough learning skills\"","quality":"real-world implication","description":"It connects the claim to a broader consequence for new drivers and everyday driving experience."}]}
